original_card.question: Does one quantified step of the proposed #4100 all-size construction hold at its actual caller?
methods: Prove one missing implication with explicit quantified hypotheses.
Find an exact counterexample at the claimed interface boundary.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Identify the proposition and what would change downstream; do not equate a finite replay with a universal proof.

first_step.inspect: Read PROOF.md and AUDIT.md in #4100. Select one distinct obligation: CRT total repair, native/free-algebra lifting, precision/conditioning, or complete fixed-tape cost. This is an author-submitted proof, not an accepted unconditional theorem.
first_step.scope: Source-binding orientation only; no scientific replay, theorem acceptance or supplier admission. Budget any heavy replay separately.

original_card.first_experiment: Check live handoffs; name one proposition, its caller, quantified domain and dependency closure. Independently prove the implication or exhibit a precise gap/counterexample. Prioritize CRT.md total repair or COMPLEX.md free-algebra lift only if unclaimed. Stop at the chosen obligation; do not substitute finite samples or root arithmetic for an all-size proof, or launch the complete package by default.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Finite supplier improvements are useful only under the retained transfer obligations.
allowed_variations: One CRT repair, native lift, precision/conditioning or tape-cost proposition, with its exact caller.
scope_change_triggers: Replacing a quantified obligation with another finite smoke test.
Treating archive intake, an author PASS receipt or a finite composed fixture as discharge of the universal hypotheses.

existing_checks.scope: PR #4100: proposed unconditional construction and finite checks, without independent acceptance.
existing_checks.remaining: Independent proof audit of one caller-bound all-size implication; all other premises remain explicit.

actual_scope: Do the narrow Neumann bounds hold for every principal section of a circular band, and does the caller's p^10 comparison follow for every integer p>=2 from its stated gap and bandwidth?
scope_change_reason: CRT total repair and the free-algebra lift already have open audits. This is the precision/conditioning obligation: INVERSE-CONDITIONING.md proves linear bands, while GAUSSIAN.md also invokes periodic axes and finite sections.
bottleneck_link: The narrow Gaussian reference uses this lemma to claim conditioning below p^10, uniform in the side length. That claim is one transfer premise of the proposed all-size construction. Proving the periodic case does not establish the Gaussian tail, truncation, or a new exponent.
stop_rule: Stop once the linear bounds, the circular-section extension, the bandwidth-free counterexample, and the p^10 arithmetic are proved. Do not derive the Gaussian tail or audit CRT.
evidence: research/narrow-neumann-section proves the three norm bounds for linear and circular bands, distinguishes the compression sentence from the arc count, and checks the p^10 plug-in for every integer p>=2 under the caller's stated hypotheses.
author: jwr
ai_assistance: Substantial assistance from the Cursor coding agent in the proof, checker and writeup.

open_questions.question: After truncation and rounding, does one explicit narrow reference meet delta>=1/(16p^2) and bandwidth < p?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The p^10 comparison is conditional on those two hypotheses. This package does not derive them from the Gaussian tail.
open_questions.first_step: Pin one prime and one truncation width, and compare the rounded row gap and the surviving bandwidth with 1/(16p^2) and p.
open_questions.blocked_by: The tail and rounding argument in GAUSSIAN.md is a separate audit.

open_questions.question: Can a filled Schur complement reuse bandwidth b, or only the inverse-norm bound?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The note invokes iterated elimination. A later step that treats the Schur complement as still bandwidth b is not given by the arc count.
open_questions.first_step: Take one explicit banded matrix, form one Schur complement, and compare its bandwidth with b and its inverse norms with the Neumann bound.
open_questions.blocked_by: No filled Schur complement is computed in this package.
